the prokaryote endonuclease can functionally replace yeast Apn1 in yeast and that the amount of endonuclesae IV required for this is much greater than that required for wild type resistance to alkylating agents.

1) the prokaryote enzyme endonuclease (Endo) IV can substitute for its yeast homolog, Apn1; 2) the hybrid protein EndoIV-Apn1 is localized to the nucleus, but it is not as active as the native enzyme in vivo; and 3) the amount of AP endonucleases required for repair of endogenous AP sites is greater than that required for repair of exogenous DNA damages.
